tex_content.html:
Proposition

↗ exer:7-13

1. ch7:7.14For a Lie group $G$ and identity neighborhood $W$, the subgroup generated by $W$ is open; if $W$ is connected it is connected; and if $G$ is connected it equals $G$.

Proof

\sketch Let $H=\langle W\rangle $ and $W_k$ be products of at most $k$ elements of $W\cup W^{-1}$. Since inversion and left translations are diffeomorphisms, induction gives that every $W_k$ and hence $H=\bigcup _kW_k$ is open. If $W$ is connected, then $W\cup W^{-1}$ and all products $W_k$ are connected, so $H$ is connected. An open subgroup is closed; therefore a connected $G$ has $H=G$.

□
